items.title: The internet's latest obsession: The end of the world
items.summary: The world seems convinced the end is near — and social media is amplifying that belief, convincing people to stock up on food, water, generators and other items. Why it matters: Online chatter is fueling viral predictions of societal collapse amid growing unease about the future. But you're probably not going to die tomorrow. What they're saying: Michael Mills, a researcher at the University of Kent who has studied doomsday prepping for more than a decade, told Axios that modern doomsday fears aren't necessarily about a specific apocalyptic scenario. "It's an overall reaction to uncertainty in most cases," Mills said. He noted that whereas Cold War-era survivalists were often focused on nuclear conflict, modern preppers worry about terrorism, climate disasters, geopolitical threats and emerging technologies. In the UK during the 1920s, Chipping Norton was the standard bearer for the favorite American pastime. At the same time Babe Ruth was leading the New York Yankees to the top of the sport across the pond, Chipping Norton were being crowned British champions in back-to-back years. But in a wait that's taken longer than the Red Sox needed to break the Curse of the Bambino, the Cotswold market town's success had never been officially recognised. Now, a century on from the team's first triumph, the championship has finally been certified by the British Baseball Federation - with a plaque celebrating the team recently unveiled at a local museum.

Using a fake DOB or leaving the field blank when making an online account can offer protection from identity theft You get a call from your bank saying there has been suspicious activity on your account. They read out your name, address and date of birth so you are happy it is a legitimate caller. But you are talking to criminals who have used your date of birth as part of a web of verifying information to convince you they are someone else. Now cybersecurity professionals have warned people to resist entering a date of birth, or to put in a fake one, to limit the amount of personal data that is online, frustrating criminals’ attempts to “jigsaw” together personal profiles.

DeMonica Amerson was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis at 21. Nearly two decades later, she received devastating news. DeMonica Amerson's diagnosis of multiple sclerosis in 2001 had been a shock. No one in her family had ever had the autoimmune condition, and it had been difficult to diagnose. Doctors had first thought she had optic neuritis because her symptoms were in her eyes. Michigan squeaked out a win over Rutgers on Saturday and dropped two spots in ESPN’s SP+ rankings as a result. Here’s where things stand heading into Week 10: For those of you who might be new to SP+, it's an advanced metric that takes into account a team's offensive, defensive, and special teams efficiencies. It combines all three metrics into one uniform metric that predicts how many points a given team would defeat (or lose to) the "average" college football team by on a neutral field. In other words, it's a metric designed to look at how "good" teams really are at different aspects of the game rather than ranking them purely on their resumes.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy described the crash, which happened near President Trump's Mar-a-Lago resort, as a "horrific tragedy". A business jet crashed in a neighbourhood in Florida on Sunday, killing all nine people on board, the US transport secretary has said. The crash happened near Cresthaven, some nine miles (14 km) from Mar-a-Lago, President Donald Trump's resort in the wealthy enclave of Palm Beach County, around 12:50 EST (17:50 GMT). Former Cardiff City captain Don Murray, who made over 500 appearances for the club, has died at the age of 80 following a long illness. The Scotland-born defender spent 13 years with the Bluebirds after joining the club in 1962, making more than 500 appearances. Murray made his debut aged 17 against Middlesbrough in 1963 and holds the club record for consecutive league appearances, having played 146 successive matches between May 1968 and November 1971. Dozens of shops across European countries have been hit by a cyber-attack affecting their fridges. Supermarkets across Europe have been hit by a suspected cyber-attack affecting their fridges and freezers, and raising concern about the vulnerabilities of internet-connected hardware from industrial machinery to humble domestic appliances. Smart devices which are connected to the internet can include fridges, central heating, and even washing machines. And while that makes them easier to control remotely, in theory, any device which goes online can potentially be exploited by malicious actors.

Colin Westby, 68, died after he suffered a medical emergency at Elland Road last month. Colin Westby was watching the match at Elland Road on Sunday 18 October when he fell ill and was taken to hospital, the club said. Posting on social media, the club said the 68-year-old was placed in a medically induced coma but, after a "period of unresponsiveness", the decision was made to withdraw life support. The club said a tribute would be held to Colin in the 68th minute of their next Premier League fixture against Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday.

The Football Association fine Luton and Barnsley £13,500 following a "mass confrontation" in last month's tie between the clubs. Jack Wilshere's Luton won 2-1 at Kenilworth Road, but a melee broke out at full-time after Barnsley's Amani Richards thought he had won a penalty only to be booked for simulation. In a statement, the FA said both sides "failed to ensure that their players and/or technical area staff did not behave in a way which was improper and/or provocative after the full-time whistle." Luton and Barnsley admitted the charges, and an independent commission ruled on imposing fines on both clubs.
